items.explanation: タ is the katakana for 'ta', the same sound as hiragana た. It is ク with one extra stroke inside.
items.mnemonic: ク folded around something: a taco with its filling.
items.culture_note: タ developed from the kanji 多.

items.explanation: チ is the katakana for 'chi', the same sound as hiragana ち. Both 'chi' and 'ti' are accepted.
items.mnemonic: A cheerleader: a short stroke for the head, arms stretched out as the crossbar, one long leg.
items.culture_note: チ developed from the kanji 千.

items.explanation: ツ is the katakana for 'tsu', the same sound as hiragana つ. It is easy to confuse with シ: in ツ the two short strokes sit on top and the long stroke falls DOWN from the top right. Both 'tsu' and 'tu' are accepted.
items.mnemonic: Two drops of water on top of a wave that falls from the top right: a tsunami coming down.
items.culture_note: ツ developed from the kanji 川.

items.explanation: テ is the katakana for 'te', the same sound as hiragana て.
items.mnemonic: A telephone pole: two crossbars and a post leaning to the left.
items.culture_note: テ developed from the kanji 天. Many long loanwords are clipped: テレビ is short for テレビジョン (terebijon, television).

items.explanation: ト is the katakana for 'to', the same sound as hiragana と.
items.mnemonic: A totem pole with one branch sticking out.
items.culture_note: ト developed from the kanji 止.
